name: NestJS
summary: A TypeScript application framework that scans a root module into a typed module graph, resolves providers through dependency injection, and adapts the initialized application to HTTP or other transports.

features.name: Decorated module graph
features.description: Nest scans a root module and recursively discovers imported modules, dynamic modules, controllers, providers, and exports into a container keyed by compiled module tokens.
benefits: Makes application composition explicit through module boundaries
Supports reusable and dynamic module assemblies
costs: Import cycles, scope, and dynamic metadata affect graph construction
The runtime graph can be larger than the entry module suggests

features.name: Container provider resolution
features.description: Nest stores providers, injectables, controllers, imports, and exports in module references and uses an instance loader and injector to create dependency-resolved instances.
benefits: Separates provider contracts from construction and scope
Allows module-local and exported dependencies to compose
costs: Resolution errors depend on visibility and provider scope
Runtime metadata adds indirection to dependency reasoning

features.name: Scanned initialization lifecycle
features.description: Nest application creation constructs a container, scans dependencies, creates provider instances, applies application providers, and then constructs an application context or transport-specific application.
benefits: Separates graph discovery from instance construction and transport startup
costs: Failures can arise in scanning, provider creation, or adapter setup

features.name: Transport adapter boundary
features.description: Nest creates applications against an abstract HTTP adapter and can select or receive an adapter implementation, separating core module and provider assembly from the concrete transport server.
benefits: Reuses application structure across supported adapters and contexts
costs: Portable module graphs remain bounded by deployment constraints

mathematical_views.model: Typed module import and export graph
mathematical_views.question: How does Nest turn a root module and metadata into reachable modules, providers, controllers, and exported dependencies?
assumptions: Modules are vertices and imports, exports, and ownership are typed edges
Dynamic modules have generated opaque keys
The graph models discovery and visibility, not provider correctness

mathematical_views.question: Which provider instances can be constructed given local providers, imports, exports, and scopes?
assumptions: Provider tokens and instances are vertices with injection edges
Reflection and asynchronous factories are abstracted

mathematical_views.model: Application initialization state machine with adapter refinement
mathematical_views.question: How does a root module progress from scan to instantiated graph and then to a concrete transport application?
assumptions: Container construction, scanning, loading, provider application, and adapter creation are ordered states
An adapter refines a transport-independent contract
The view does not claim behavioral equivalence among adapters

costs: Metadata-driven construction increases runtime and tooling complexity

benefits: Construction and visibility are separated from consumers
costs: Scope and metadata can obscure dependency paths

benefits: Discovery, construction, and setup have distinct phases
costs: Large graphs increase startup time and phase-specific failures

benefits: Core composition can be reused across transports
costs: Portability is bounded by adapter behavior
